Depost AI 2 is out: what we changed and why

We rebuilt Depost AI from scratch. It took eight months. This is what the new version does, what it costs, and why we did it this way.
Atta-Ur-Rehman Shah · September 14, 2026 · 3 min read

We shipped Depost AI 2 last week. It is the biggest thing our small team has done, and I wanted to write it up here on the studio blog too, because a lot of people know Depost AI without knowing the company behind it.
The short version: we rebuilt the whole product from scratch. It took eight months. The price did not change. It is live now at depost.ai .

Why we started over

The first Depost AI came out of beta in June 2025. It was a set of AI writing tools. You picked one, filled in a form and got a post back. Thousands of people used it, and we learned a lot from them.
The feedback was consistent. Nobody complained about the writing. What took people’s time was everything around the writing. Deciding what to post about. Making a graphic. Picking a time. Remembering to reply. Finding out a week later whether any of it had worked.
The requests we got most often were about approvals, workspaces, teams and a chat. The old product was not built to carry any of that. We could have bolted the pieces on. We decided to start again instead.

What the new version does

You connect your LinkedIn account. Then you talk to it, the way you would message a colleague. “Plan my week.” “Write a post about the thing I told you yesterday.” “Which of my posts did best last month?”
Behind that chat are four helpers. We call them agents. One reads your analytics. One comes up with ideas. One writes in your voice, learned from what you have already published. One makes the graphics in your own colours. You do not have to think about which one is working. You just ask.

seltz.title: About us
seltz.snippet:
Depost AI started as a private system. Atta had spent years on LinkedIn doing what everyone does, posting, liking, and scrolling, with plenty of activity and no pipeline to show for it. Growth only came when he stopped starting from a blank page every morning and built context instead: what works in the niche, what sounds like him, and what the numbers say to do next.

The system worked, and it was miserable to run by hand. Seven tools, twenty open tabs, and a spreadsheet holding it all together. So we built the workspace we wanted: one place that learns your voice, studies your niche, drafts the posts, designs the visuals, and plans the week. It was our own solution before it was a product. It turned out a lot of creators were stuck exactly where we had been.

We keep the team at three on purpose. The product is the growth team, everything on our own LinkedIn runs through it first, and everything you send through the contact page lands with one of the people below.
